trust_decision.summary: Whether a token value can reach the log line unescaped is decided in two places: the character class of escapeLogField() and whether the token was registered through the token() wrapper; at the pinned commit only :remote-user is escaped and its character class stops at \u001f/\u007f.

landing_point.why: The summary names unescaped Unicode line separators, and the pinned tree already runs escapeLogField() over :remote-user, so an engineer reads the regex character class first: U+0085/U+2028/U+2029 are one character-class edit away and that edit alone reproduces the reported payload.

fix_sites.entry_point: morgan(':remote-user') over an HTTP request carrying Authorization: Basic ... (the built-in remote-user token)
morgan.token(name, fn) public registration API, whose result is consumed by both morgan(fmtString) and morgan(fmtFunction)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: token() is registration plumbing that only stores the callback, so a solver can argue the escaping belongs in the handful of built-in tokens that read request data and that the wrapper, and every application-registered token, needs no change.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A format function may return a plain object and that object must be written to an objectMode stream untouched (asserted as a deep-equal object at test/morgan.js:1225) and stringified as '[object Object]' otherwise (test/morgan.js:1250); escaping or coercing the assembled line at the write path destroys both.

O6_input_shapes: Basic-auth username containing C1/Unicode separators (U+0085 NEL, U+2028, U+2029), the payload the fix's :remote-user test uses
request header value containing a C1 control via :req[x-test], including the header value delivered as an array and joined at index.js:387-389
the same header value read through a function format via tokens.req(req, res, 'x-test') instead of a format string
non-string token returns (numeric :status / :res[content-length], undefined tokens) that must pass through the wrapper unchanged because the wrapper only escapes typeof string

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new built-in header token (:host, :query, :origin, ...) returning req.headers[...] raw, exactly like :referrer and :user-agent
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: every built-in token in this file is a bare getter (index.js:250-407) and only :remote-user escapes, so a maintainer adding a token writes the same raw-return line and relies on the token() wrapper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second, structured output path (a built-in JSON format or an objectMode serialization step) that emits field values without passing through token()
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: objectMode pass-through landed in the commit immediately before the pinned one (51007f9) and the README documents objects written as-is, so a maintainer extending that feature would naturally emit raw request values.

O9_family: log injection / improper output neutralization for logs (CWE-117)

O10_build.toolchain: npm; no compile step; mocha 10.8.2 + supertest 4.0.2 + split for tests, nyc + eslint 6 for coverage/lint
O10_build.project_tests: test/morgan.js (~1900 lines, mocha+supertest against a loopback http/https server) and test/noColor.js; `npm test` runs both in separate processes (package.json:51). :remote-user escaping is already covered at test/morgan.js:559-696 (CRLF, null, tab/ESC, backslash, full forging payload, and exact escaped output) and dev colour at test/morgan.js:1387-1425 via expandColorCharacters (test/morgan.js:1833-1836).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Extend the character class at index.js:64 (or escape the assembled line in the write path): the first fixes the reported :remote-user payload but leaves the other tokens, function formats and application-registered tokens raw, while the second breaks objectMode pass-through and the dev format's raw ANSI colours.

out_of_scope_notes: getFormatFunction falls back to compiling the format name itself when it is unknown (index.js:513-515), so passing request-derived data as the format argument yields an attacker-influenced format string and forged literals; that is outside this advisory's token-value property and was not pursued.
